title: Clean Romance Books Like Bridgerton | Regency Reads Without the Steam
kicker: A reading guide from Emma Velott
desc: Loved the ballrooms, dukes and gossip of Bridgerton but want your romance closed-door? A guide to clean Regency romance books like Bridgerton, with where to start.
lead: You finished the latest season, or perhaps the books, and you want more of it. The ballrooms and the scandal sheets, the dukes who are far too sure of themselves, the heroines who are cleverer than anyone gives them credit for. What you would like a little less of is the steam. This guide is for you.
books_heading: Emma's clean Regency romances to start with

books.why: Opens with a public jilting in a crowded ballroom, which is about as Bridgerton as a first chapter gets, then moves to a remote estate and a duke who has stopped letting anyone look at him. Start here if you loved the Simon and Daphne slow burn.
A grumpy duke, a widow with a temper and a marriage nobody planned. If Anthony and Kate's sparring was your favourite part, this one has the same push and pull.
A shorter read with a reformed-rake hero, one bed and a snowstorm. Good for a single cosy evening.

paras: Most of the pleasure of Bridgerton comes from the world around the couple. There is the marriage mart with its rules and its quiet cruelty, the families who meddle, the gossip that can ruin a girl by breakfast, and the strange freedom of two people who are only allowed to speak honestly when nobody else is listening. The romance works because the rules are so tight. A glance across a ballroom carries weight when a glance is all anyone is permitted.

Then there are the heroes. Dukes, viscounts and the occasional rake who has been running from something for years and is finally caught. Readers come back for the moment such a man realises the woman in front of him has seen straight through his armour and is not in the least impressed by it.

sections.h2: Why some readers want a clean version
paras: Julia Quinn's novels and the Netflix series both include open-door love scenes. Plenty of readers enjoy them, and plenty would rather skip ahead, read on a train without angling the screen away, or pass a book to a mother or daughter without a warning attached. Clean Regency romance keeps the setting, the banter and the longing and leaves the bedroom door shut.

Clean does not have to mean bland. The tension in a closed-door book has to come from somewhere, so it comes from the arrangement that cannot be broken, the conversation that keeps getting interrupted, and the hand held a moment longer than it should be. Many readers find that slow burn more romantic, since the wait is half the fun.

sections.h2: What to look for in a clean Bridgerton read-alike
paras: A Regency or late-Georgian setting, roughly 1795 to 1837, with the season, country houses and a strict idea of what is proper. A hero with a title and a reason to keep people at a distance. A heroine who has something to lose, which might be her reputation, her income or her family's good name. A trope with built-in tension, such as a marriage of convenience, a fake engagement, forced proximity or enemies who are obliged to be civil. And a firm happily-ever-after, because nobody reads this genre to be left heartbroken.
Look for the words clean, sweet, closed-door or fade-to-black in the description. Those all mean the romance stays on the page and the intimacy happens off it.

sections.h2: Other clean Regency authors worth reading
paras: If you want to build a whole shelf, Georgette Heyer more or less invented the Regency romance and her books are witty, clean and still in print. Julie Klassen writes longer, more atmospheric clean historical novels with a gentle faith element. Sarah M. Eden and Martha Keyes both write sweet Regency romance series with families you can follow from book to book. Emma's books sit alongside these, with a little more emotional weight and heroes who have been through something.

faq.a: No. Julia Quinn's Bridgerton novels include open-door love scenes, as does the Netflix series. Clean Regency romance keeps a similar setting and tone with the intimacy kept off the page.
A closed-door romance has kissing and plenty of romantic tension, but any love scenes happen off the page. The story fades out at the bedroom door and picks up afterwards.

faq.q: Which Emma Velott book should I read first if I liked Bridgerton?
faq.a: A Jilted Bride for the Battle-Scarred Duke. It opens at a society ball and turns into a slow-burn romance with a reclusive duke. You can read the prologue free on this site.

faq.q: Do I need to read Emma's books in order?
faq.a: No. Each book is a standalone with its own couple and a complete happily-ever-after.

title: Marriage of Convenience Regency Romance Books (Clean) | Emma Velott
kicker: A reading guide from Emma Velott
desc: Clean marriage of convenience Regency romance books, from arranged matches to fake marriages. Why readers love the trope and where to start with Emma Velott.
lead: Two people marry for every reason except love. A debt, a scandal, an heir, a roof over someone's head. Then they have to live together, and the arrangement that looked so sensible on paper starts to give way. Few tropes suit the Regency better.
books_heading: Marriages of convenience by Emma Velott

books.why: A widow takes a housekeeping post with a cold duke, and what starts as an arrangement becomes a marriage neither of them meant to want. Grumpy hero, outspoken heroine and a secret that will not stay buried.
The fake-marriage version. A governess and a rake pose as husband and wife at a snowbound inn to save her reputation, with strict rules about which side of the bed is whose.
Not a marriage of convenience at the start, but built from the same slow, reluctant closeness, as a jilted bride takes a position in a reclusive duke's household.

sections.h2: Why the trope works so well in the Regency
paras: In 1815 marriage really was a practical matter. Women had few ways to support themselves, estates needed heirs, debts had to be paid and a single rumour could close every door in town. A marriage made for sensible reasons was ordinary, which means the trope never feels forced in a Regency setting. The characters are doing what everyone around them does.

The romance comes from the gap between the contract and the people. They agreed to separate rooms and civil breakfasts. Nobody agreed to notice how the other takes their tea, or to worry when they come home late, or to feel that small jolt when a hand brushes a sleeve on the stairs.

sections.h2: The different flavours of the trope
paras: An arranged match is decided by families or circumstance before the couple have much say. A marriage of convenience proper is chosen by the couple themselves, usually because each has something the other needs. A fake marriage or pretend engagement is a performance for the outside world, which brings the added danger of being found out. A compromised marriage happens when the couple are caught in a situation that leaves society no other answer.
Each one creates the same delicious problem. The couple are bound together long before they trust each other, and the story is about closing that gap.

sections.h2: What makes a good clean marriage of convenience
paras: In a closed-door book the wedding night is not the turning point, so the emotional milestones carry the weight. The first real conversation. The first time one of them defends the other in public. The moment one realises the other has been quietly kind for weeks without saying so. Readers who love this trope tend to love the in-between scenes, the shared meals and the letters and the evenings by the fire, more than any grand declaration.
Emma writes these marriages slowly on purpose, so the happily-ever-after feels earned.

faq.q: What is a marriage of convenience romance?
faq.a: A romance where the couple marry for practical reasons, such as money, reputation or an heir, and fall in love afterwards. It is one of the most popular tropes in historical romance.

faq.q: Are Emma Velott's marriage of convenience books clean?
faq.a: Yes. All of Emma's books are clean, closed-door Regency romances with a happily-ever-after.

faq.q: What is the difference between a fake marriage and a marriage of convenience?
faq.a: In a marriage of convenience the couple are really married. In a fake marriage they only pretend to be, which adds the risk of being discovered. The Rakish Viscount's Pretend Wife is a fake marriage story.

title: Scarred Hero Romance Books | Clean Wounded Duke Regency Romance
kicker: A reading guide from Emma Velott
desc: Clean scarred hero and wounded duke Regency romance. Battle-scarred dukes, reclusive heroes and the heroines who refuse to look away. Where to start with Emma Velott.
lead: He came home from the war with a face he no longer shows anyone, or a wound nobody can see. He has shut up the house and stopped going to town. Then someone arrives who will not keep to the rooms she has been given, and will not pretend she has not noticed him. Readers come back to the scarred hero again and again, and for good reason.

books.why: Ronan Kingsford, Duke of Penwythe, came home from the war with a hand that will not close and has not let anyone past his gates in four years. Ariana, freshly jilted in front of three hundred guests, has her own reasons to avoid being looked at. A slow, tender Beauty and the Beast kind of romance.
The wounds here are of the hidden kind. A duke who has emptied his own house and a widow who sees that his coldness is armour.

sections.h2: Why readers love a scarred hero
paras: The scarred hero is a man who has decided he is unlovable and arranged his whole life around that belief. The romance is the slow dismantling of it. He expects pity or revulsion and gets neither. He expects her to leave and she stays. Every small act of ordinary attention lands harder because he had stopped expecting any.

It is also a trope about seeing clearly. The heroine is usually the first person in years to look at him properly, scars and temper and all, and decide he is worth the trouble. Many readers find that more romantic than any amount of flawless good looks.

The Regency sits right at the end of the Napoleonic Wars, which ended at Waterloo in 1815. Thousands of officers came home with injuries that changed how society saw them, and plenty of them were heirs to great estates. That history gives the wounded duke a real foundation. His retreat from the ballroom makes sense, and so does his fear of being stared at by people who once admired him.
Hidden wounds work just as well. Grief, guilt, a betrayal that left him guarded. The scar does not have to be on his face for the story to work.

sections.h2: The heroine who will not look away
paras: The best scarred-hero heroines are not nurses or saints. They are women with their own troubles who happen to be stubborn, kind or simply too tired to be afraid of him. Ariana in A Jilted Bride has just been humiliated in public, and she recognises a fellow hider when she meets one. Their story is about two people who have both been looked at the wrong way learning to be looked at the right way.

faq.q: What is a scarred hero romance?
faq.a: A romance where the hero carries a physical or emotional wound, often from war, that has made him withdraw from the world. The heroine draws him back out.

faq.q: Is A Jilted Bride for the Battle-Scarred Duke a Beauty and the Beast retelling?
faq.a: It has the same shape, with a reclusive, scarred duke in a remote house and a heroine who refuses to be frightened of him, but it is an original clean Regency romance.
Yes. Emma's scarred hero romances are closed-door, with a happily-ever-after.

title: Grumpy Duke Romance Books | Clean Grumpy Sunshine Regency Romance
kicker: A reading guide from Emma Velott
desc: Clean grumpy duke romance, where a cold, scowling duke meets a heroine who refuses to be frightened of him. Grumpy sunshine Regency romance by Emma Velott.
lead: He scowls. He dismisses staff with a look. He has a reputation in three counties for being impossible. And then a woman walks into his house who simply does not care, and tells him so. The grumpy duke is one of the most satisfying heroes in Regency romance, mostly because of what happens when he finally softens.

books.why: The Duke of Wrenwick has frightened off every servant he ever had. Anastasia lasts three days before telling him exactly what his temper costs him. The purest grumpy duke on Emma's shelf.
Ronan is less cross and more withdrawn, a duke who would like everyone to leave him alone. For readers who like their grumpy hero wounded underneath.

sections.h2: Why readers love a grumpy hero
paras: A grumpy hero is a promise. Somewhere under all that scowling is a man who cares a great deal and has decided it is safer not to show it, and the story will eventually prove it. Readers enjoy the sparring on the way there, and they especially enjoy the small cracks, such as the first reluctant smile, the gift he pretends was an accident, or the moment he loses his temper on her behalf instead of at her.
The grumpy duke adds power to the mix. He is used to being obeyed. A heroine who will not obey, and who has good reasons, unsettles his whole world in a way that is very fun to read.

sections.h2: Grumpy and sunshine, or grumpy and fiery
paras: The classic pairing is grumpy and sunshine, a sour hero and a warm, optimistic heroine. Emma tends to write the other version, where the heroine has a temper of her own and has run out of patience for powerful men who behave badly. Both work. The sunshine heroine wins him by kindness and the fiery heroine wins him by refusing to back down, and either way he never quite recovers.

sections.h2: What keeps a grumpy duke romantic
paras: A grumpy hero needs a reason. Grief, a betrayal, a responsibility he took on too young. Without one he is just rude. The best grumpy dukes are cold to the world and quietly decent in private, and the heroine is the first to notice the difference. In a clean romance that slow reveal carries the whole story, so every softened word counts.

faq.q: What is a grumpy duke romance?
faq.a: A historical romance where the hero is a cold, short-tempered or forbidding duke who is gradually won over by the heroine. It is often paired with the grumpy sunshine trope.

faq.q: Which Emma Velott book has the grumpiest duke?
faq.a: A Fiery Widow for the Cold Duke. The Duke of Wrenwick has emptied his own house of staff by the time the heroine arrives.
Yes. They are closed-door Regency romances with a happily-ever-after.

title: Sweet Historical Romance Books (Clean Regency) | Emma Velott
kicker: A reading guide from Emma Velott
desc: What sweet and clean historical romance means, how it differs from closed-door and steamy romance, and the best clean Regency romance books to start with.
lead: Sweet, clean, closed-door, fade-to-black. Readers and retailers use all of these words, and they do not always mean quite the same thing. Here is a plain guide to what each one means in historical romance, and how to find the books that suit you.
books_heading: Clean Regency romances by Emma Velott

books.why: A slow-burn, emotional romance with a scarred duke. Kisses and longing on the page, nothing more.
A grumpy duke and a widow, a marriage of convenience and a good deal of sparring. Closed-door.
A light, funny novella about a fake marriage at a snowbound inn. They share a bed and keep to their own sides of it.

paras: Sweet romance usually means kisses only, with no love scenes on or off the page and very mild language. Clean romance is close to the same thing and is the word most readers search for. Closed-door means the couple may well have a wedding night, but the story stops at the bedroom door and picks up the next morning. Fade-to-black means much the same as closed-door.
Emma's books are clean and closed-door. There is longing, there are kisses, and married couples are allowed to be married, but nothing explicit appears on the page and the language stays gentle.

sections.h2: Why so many readers choose clean historical romance
paras: Some readers simply prefer it. Others want books they can share with family, read on a commute or recommend to a book club without a caveat. Many say the slow build of a clean romance is more satisfying, since every touch matters when there are so few of them.

The Regency is especially well suited to clean romance. Its manners were strict, a couple might go weeks without being alone together, and a dance or a walk in the garden could carry enormous meaning. The period does half the work of building tension.

sections.h2: Popular tropes in sweet historical romance
paras: Marriage of convenience, fake engagement, the reformed rake, the wounded or grumpy duke, the governess or companion in a great house, enemies to lovers and forced proximity are all favourites. You will find several of them in Emma's books, and each has its own reading guide on this site.

faq.q: What is the difference between sweet and clean romance?
faq.a: The terms overlap. Sweet romance usually means kisses only, while clean romance can include married intimacy as long as it happens off the page. Both avoid explicit scenes.

faq.q: Are Emma Velott's books sweet or clean?
faq.a: Clean and closed-door. There are kisses and romantic tension, and anything more happens off the page.

faq.q: Where can I buy Emma Velott's books?
faq.a: Directly from this website as EPUB and PDF ebooks that work on any device, or on Kobo.
